why: Every element is in or out, so there are 2^n subsets; the only work is listing them in the required order (by size, then by index positions), which is exactly combinations of each size k in index order.
hints: How many choices does each element have, and so how many subsets are there in total?

The ordering asks for all subsets of size 0, then size 1, and so on, with same-size subsets ordered by their index positions. That is 'all combinations of k indices in lexicographic order' for k = 0..n.
For k in 0..n, generate combinations of size k by backtracking (choose the next index greater than the last) or itertools.combinations, keeping nums' order. O(n * 2^n).
pitfalls: Keep elements in input order inside a subset ([3,-1], not [-1,3]); do not sort nums.
The usual include/exclude DFS produces a different order; group by size as required.
